Catalog · fragile context packs

The fragile context atlas.

Companies are already putting fragile knowledge into RAG, chatbots, copilots, enterprise search, and agent memory. Most don’t know which parts are stale, conflicting, jurisdiction-specific, source-dependent, or unsafe to serve. This atlas catalogs those fragile context surfaces by domain and failure mode — and links the ones Baltor already governs end-to-end.

The fragile part isn’t always the document. It’s the answer derived from it — “refund window is 30 days” can be true in an old wiki and false in the billing system, a contract override, or a regulated dispute window.
Fragility is one lens — not the whole engine.

Catching stale & conflicting context is one thing Baltor does. It sits beside the rest of the governed-context engine — every served pack is reconciled, hardened, enhanced, optimized, and verified, with receipts and source handles. This atlas tags the fragility; the demos show the full pipeline.

⇄ Reconcile conflicts → one answer △ Harden fragile facts → refreshable objects ➕ Enhance with citations & context ◇ Optimize → token-lean cited packs ✓ Verify → receipts + provenance

How this hub relates to Baltor. OpenContextHub catalogs reference context packs and their fragility — it is not a truth authority. Baltor governs context before consumption: it decomposes a pack into atomic facts, holds out conflicts, tracks freshness, preserves source handles and receipts, and serves only what is supported.
